title: `AVG` of integers: a `DOUBLE` from the exact sum
verdict: `DOUBLE`; exact integer sum, one division (in `long double` for `INTEGER` and `BIGINT`)
description: `avg` has one overload per integer width it names, `SMALLINT`, `INTEGER`, `BIGINT` and `HUGEINT`, and each returns `DOUBLE`; there is no integer result. `TINYINT` has none: the binder takes the overload with the cheapest implicit cast, and a cast to `BIGINT` costs 101 against 110 for `SMALLINT`, so `avg(TINYINT)` runs the `BIGINT` one.

`SMALLINT`: the sum is an `int64_t` (`RegularAdd`, unchecked, out of reach below 2^48 rows) and the result `double(sum) / double(count)`. `INTEGER` and `BIGINT`: the sum is an exact `HUGEINT` (`AddToHugeint`) and the result `long double(sum) / long double(count)`, rounded to `DOUBLE`. `long double` is 80-bit on x86-64 Linux and the same as `double` on arm64 macOS and MSVC, so the last bit of a large mean can depend on the platform.
No values gives NULL. The width dispatch is one template instantiation per width (`GetAverageAggregate`), which is what lets this reading cover `i8` to `i64`.
reference: `avg_int_result` follows the plan's declared output type (#209). With `fp64` the reference averages the integers' conversions to doubles (`parseMeasure`), so it rounds each value and then the sum, where DuckDB rounds the exact sum once; both are within #85's bound.

With `i64` the reference is the exact mean truncated toward zero (`AggFn.iavg`); sverify's DuckDB SQL writes it as `CAST(SUM(v) // COUNT(v) AS BIGINT)` (`sql/duckdb.py`, `int_avg`), on the exact `HUGEINT` sum, so DuckDB's `AVG` is not used there.
